Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

innovation noun

also innovations, innovative, innovate, something new

classical

Cic. Mur. 61: inventa Zēnōnis (Lewis & Short)
Ov. M. 1.521: inventum medicīna meum est (Lewis & Short)

inventum, inventī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a device, invention, discovery

A thing devised: a new method, a new idea.

Other words

  • novitās, novitātis f. — newness, novelty

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.60: reī novitās (Lewis & Short); Quint. 9.2.66: ipsā novitāte ac varietāte magis dēlectat (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • novō, novāre, novāvī, novātum — renew; introduce something new, innovate

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 5.10.106: multa novantur in omnī genere māteriae (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    But rēs novāre and rēs novae are political: to overthrow the government, revolution (Liv. 1.52) (Lewis & Short).

  • innovātiō, innovātiōnis f. — a renewing, an alteration

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Tert. adv. Marc. 1.1 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Late Latin; inventum and novitās say it classically.

Examples

  • inventum medicīna meum est

    medicine is my inventionOv. M. 1.521 (Lewis & Short)

See also new.
